chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Sufyan, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, who said:

Ibn al-Kawa' said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Commander of the Faithful, what do you make of your saying: 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab'? He (peace be upon him) said: Woe to you, O One-Eyed! It is the gathering of scattered things, the raising of the dead, the harvesting of vegetation, and calamities upon calamities, destroying and annihilating; neither I nor you will be there.

key_terms.أَعْوَرَ: Al-A'war (The One-Eyed, a nickname for Ibn al-Kawa')

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's saying 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates his enigmatic phrase 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab' as a period of intense cosmic and earthly upheaval characterized by the gathering of scattered resources, resurrection of the dead, and successive calamities. This interpretation highlights the transient nature of worldly power and life, emphasizing that both the Imam and his interlocutor, Ibn al-Kawa', will perish during this era of destruction, underscoring the inevitability of divine decree and the temporary nature of human existence.

en.basel-kadem: 80.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukair, from Zurara, that he said:

I went, me and Bukair, along with a man from the sons of Ali to the cites until we reached Uhud. He then showed us the graves of the martyrs. He then made us enter the path, and we went with him for an hour until we went to a mosque there. He said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, prayed in it. Hence, we prayed in it, and then he showed us a place at the top of the mountain, and he said: The Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family climbed to it, and it used to be rain water there. Zurara said: It then hit within me that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, did not climb to any water. I then said: I will not come with you. I will sleep here until you come. Then he and Bukair walked, and so they went and then came to me, and then we all went. Then, until the next day, we came to Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, and he said to us: Where were you yesterday, for indeed, I did not see you? So, we informed him and described to him the mosque and the spot in which it was claimed that the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, climbed to and and washed his face in. Abu Ja’far said: The Messenger of Allah never came to that place. We said to him: It has also been narrated to us that his front tooth were broken. He said: No. Allah took him unto Himself in safety, however, he was cut open in his face, and he sent Ali, so he brought him water in a leather vessel, and the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, felt disgusted to drink from it, and he washed his face.
